A_core_direct_lifespan.title: The mTOR pathway is necessary for survival of mice with short telomeres.
evidence_quotes: 3-month-old wild type and second-generation telomerase-deﬁcient mice (G2 Terc−/−) in a C57BL/6 genetic background14 were fed with either control chow or chow- containing encapsulated rapamycin at 42 ppm (mg of drug per kg of food)31.

We found that rapamycin treatment increased median longevity of wild-type mice (Terc+/+) by 39%, resulting in a median longevity of 26.5 months in rapamycin-fed Terc+/+ mice compared to only 19 months in the control-fed cohorts (Fig. 1b).

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Rapamycin extends murine lifespan but has limited effects on aging.
evidence_quotes: we performed to determine whether rapamycin slows the rate of aging in male C57BL/6J mice.

Survival analysis applied to all treated cohorts, and lifespan extension by rapamycin was demonstrated relative to corresponding vehicle controls (Figure 1), confirming previously reported longevity effects (8–11).

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Health Effects of Long-Term Rapamycin Treatment: The Impact on Mouse Health of Enteric Rapamycin Treatment from Four Months of Age throughout Life.
evidence_quotes: At four months of age 160 mice, 80 animals per sex, began receiving mouse chow (Purina 5LG6) containing either microencapsulated rapamycin (14 ppm) or empty capsules (eudragit = control), (n = 40 animals per sex and treatment group).
Consistent with our previous findings, survival of both males and females was modestly enhanced in YF animals [35].

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Transient rapamycin treatment during developmental stage extends lifespan in Mus musculus and Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin (10 mg/kg) was administered daily in two distinct temporal windows, from postnatal day 4 to postnatal day 30 (P4‐P30), or from postnatal day 30 to postnatal day 60 (P30‐P60)
Combined data from both sexes showed a 9.6% increase in median lifespan in P4‐P30 rapamycin‐treated mice compared with control mice (treated with ethanol)

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: BMAL1-dependent regulation of the mTOR signaling pathway delays aging.
evidence_quotes: treatment with the mTORC1 inhibitor rapamycin increased lifespan of Bmal1−/− mice by 50%
we decided to compare activity of mTOR signaling in cells isolated from wild type and BMAL1-deficient mice

A_core_direct_lifespan.title: Dose-dependent effects of mTOR inhibition on weight and mitochondrial disease in mice.
evidence_quotes: we compared the effects of dietary rapamycin at doses ranging from 14 to 378 PPM on developmental weight in control and Ndufs4 knockout mice and on health and survival in the Ndufs4 knockout model.

The highest oral dose, approximately 27-times the dose shown to extend murine lifespan, increased survival in Ndufs4 knockout mice similarly to daily rapamycin injection without observable adverse effects.

B_disease_model_survival.title: Premature recruitment of oocyte pool and increased mTOR activity in Fmr1 knockout mice and reversal of phenotype with rapamycin.
evidence_quotes: Breeding, histologic and mTOR signaling data were obtained at multiple time points in KO and wild type (WT) mice fed a control or rapamycin (mTOR inhibitor) diet.

Reversal of phenotypes and protein levels in rapamycin-treated KO mice, as well as increased reproductive lifespan of rapamycin-fed WT mice, suggest the mTOR pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

B_disease_model_survival.title: Acarbose suppresses symptoms of mitochondrial disease in a mouse model of Leigh syndrome.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin, a drug that increases lifespan and health during normative ageing, also increases survival and reduces neurological symptoms in a mouse model of the severe mitochondrial disease Leigh syndrome.
Furthermore, rapamycin and acarbose have additive effects in delaying neurological symptoms and increasing maximum lifespan in Ndufs4 −/− mice.

B_disease_model_survival.title: Rapamycin extends lifespan and delays tumorigenesis in heterozygous p53+/- mice.
evidence_quotes: Mice of the first group (n=37) were given rapamycin in drinking water (approximately 1.5 mg/kg per day), whereas mice of the second group (n=38) were given tap water without rapamycin and served as control.
In rapamycin-treated mice, the mean lifespan was 410 days and lifespan of the last 10% of survivals could not be determined (Fig. 1 A ).

B_disease_model_survival.title: Rapamycin increases lifespan and inhibits spontaneous tumorigenesis in inbred female mice.
evidence_quotes: Daily administration of rapamycin, an inhibitor of the nutrient sensing mechanistic target of rapamycin complex I (mTORC1), rescues multiple manifestations of mitochondrial disease in Ndufs4 −/− mice, including neurological symptoms, accumulation of glycolytic intermediates and lactate, loss of body fat, aberrant nutrient and growth factor signalling, and survival
Furthermore, rapamycin and acarbose have additive effects in delaying neurological symptoms and increasing maximum lifespan in Ndufs4 −/− mice.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Metformin potentiates nephrotoxicity by promoting NETosis in response to renal ferroptosis.
evidence_quotes: we treated mice with AKI induced by renal ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) with different drugs alone. Notably, nicotinamide, resveratrol, rapamycin, and senolytics, but not metformin, showed some to no protective effects on AKI based on various readouts of renal health and func- tion
a higher dose of metformin (200 mg/kg) resulted in 100% lethality of I/R mice while the untreated I/R mice showed 100% survival
demote_reasons:
manual:resolved_excluded: Off-topic for primary lifespan corpus. Paper studies metformin-driven
nephrotoxicity in acute kidney injury (AKI); rapamycin appears only as
one of several comparator drugs tested for protective effect against
I/R-induced renal damage. The "100% survival" quoted refers to AKI
survival over days, not lifespan extension.

C_secondary_contextual.title: High-content screening identifies ganoderic acid A as a senotherapeutic to prevent cellular senescence and extend healthspan in preclinical models.
evidence_quotes: As expected, rapamycin (100 μM) signiﬁcantly extended the median (12%) and maximum lifespan (25%) of C. elegans (Fig. 2e).

Upon stimulating aged worms at 30 °C, treatments with rapamycin and GAA extended the mean lifespan by 23% and 35% and the maximum lifespan by 9% and 12% respectively, compared to those treated with DMSO treatment (Fig. 2f).

C_secondary_contextual.title: Lifespan-extending interventions induce consistent patterns of fatty acid oxidation in mouse livers.
evidence_quotes: In this LC-M001 experiment, 48 mice were either untreated (Control) or subjected to one of three lifespan- extending drug treatments (ACA, 17aE2, or Rapa)

ACA, 17aE2, and Rapa showed signiﬁcantly higher RCI median in the examined modules compared to Control (Fig. 2a, Supplementary Fig. 1a), suggesting general tightening of module proﬁles by each of these lifespan-extending interventions.
demote_reasons: no quote names a primary intervention term

C_secondary_contextual.title: Long-lasting geroprotection from brief rapamycin treatment in early adulthood by persistently increased intestinal autophagy.
evidence_quotes: In mice, a 3-month, early treatment also induced a memory effect, with maintenance similar to chronic treatment, of lysozyme distribution, Man2B1 level in intestinal crypts, Paneth cell architecture and gut barrier function, even 6 months after rapamycin was withdrawn.
In Drosophila, a brief, early rapamycin treatment of adults extended lifespan and attenuated age-related decline in the intestine to the same degree as lifelong dosing.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Inhibition of S6K lowers age-related inflammation and increases lifespan through the endolysosomal system.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin treatment also elevated Syntaxin 12/13 levels in mouse liver and prevented age-related increase in noncanonical NF-κB signaling

Suppression of TORC1 signaling genetically or pharmacologically by the US Food and Drug Administration-licensed drug rapamycin (Rapa), promotes lifespan and healthspan in various model organisms including nematode worms, fruit flies and mice
demote_reasons: no quote names a control term

C_secondary_contextual.title: The geroprotectors trametinib and rapamycin combine additively to extend mouse healthspan and lifespan.
evidence_quotes: We measured the survival of mice on diets contain- ing only rapamycin (42 mg kg–1), the dose so far inducing the largest increase in longevity20, or both rapamycin (42 mg kg–1) and trametinib (1.44 mg kg–1).

intermittent rapamycin treatment extended lifespan in both sexes to a similar extent (P < 0.0001, log-rank test; P = 0.2481 for the sex–drug interaction, Cox proportional hazard) with an increase in median and maximum lifespan of 17.4% and 16.5%, respectively, in female mice (Fig. 2b) and 16.6% and 18.3%, respectively, in male mice (Fig. 2c).

C_secondary_contextual.title: Diverse interventions that extend mouse lifespan suppress shared age-associated epigenetic changes at critical gene regulatory regions.
evidence_quotes: One cohort was given encapsulated rapamycin (42 parts per million (ppm)) from 4 months of age
Dietary and drug interventions that extend lifespan include calorie restriction (CR) and the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin

C_secondary_contextual.title: Epigenetic aging signatures in mice livers are slowed by dwarfism, calorie restriction and rapamycin treatment.
evidence_quotes: we analyzed 28 additional methylomes from mice subjected to lifespan-extending conditions, including Prop1df/df dwarfism, calorie restriction or dietary rapamycin.
We found that mice treated with these lifespan-extending interventions were significantly younger in epigenetic age than their untreated, wild-type age-matched controls.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Mice fed rapamycin have an increase in lifespan associated with major changes in the liver transcriptome.
evidence_quotes: Two dietary regimens were used in this study: mice fed a commercial chow, LabDiet 5LG6-JL (LabDiet, St. Louis, MO), with Eudragit capsule (control) or 14 ppm encapsulated rapamycin (Rapa) in the food

Rapamycin was found to increase (11% to 16%) the lifespan of male and female C57BL/6J mice most likely by reducing the increase in the hazard for mortality (i.e., the rate of aging) term in the Gompertz mortality analysis.

C_secondary_contextual.title: Rapamycin doses sufficient to extend lifespan do not compromise muscle mitochondrial content or endurance.
evidence_quotes: Therefore, we tested whether rapamycin, at the same doses used to extend lifespan, affects mitochondrial function in skeletal muscle.

In agreement with the lack of change in mitochondrial components, rapamycin-treated mice had endurance equivalent to that of untreated controls, and isolated, permeabilized muscle fibers displayed similar rates of oxygen consumption.
demote_reasons:
manual:resolved_excluded: Side-effect / mechanism study, not a primary lifespan-extension trial.
The paper uses rapamycin at "lifespan-extending doses" to ask whether
muscle mitochondrial content / endurance are compromised. Lifespan is
referenced as a known prior result, not measured here.

C_secondary_contextual.title: p53 and rapamycin are additive.
evidence_quotes: Mice were fed chow containing empty Eudragit capsules (control) or capsules containing 14 ppm eRapa, the concentration previously shown to extend lifespan, delay tumor-related death, retard a number of age-related pathologies, and improve cerebral function
eRapa extended the median survival of p53+/- (520 to 582 days, p=0.0522) and p53+/+ mice (681 to 802.5 days, p=0.0013).
demote_reasons: no quote names a primary intervention term

C_secondary_contextual.title: SRN-901, a Novel Longevity Drug, Extends Lifespan and Healthspan by Targeting Multiple Aging Pathways.
evidence_quotes: Rapamycin was mixed in food with a concentration of 14.4 ppm.
While rapamycin increased lifespan in adult mice, nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotinamide riboside (NR) did not show significant differences in median lifespan compared to placebo.
demote_reasons:
manual:resolved_excluded: SRN-901 (a novel compound) is the primary intervention; rapamycin is a
positive-control comparator. Per pre-specified PICO ("primary
intervention = rapamycin/sirolimus"), this is comparator usage, not a
primary rapamycin trial.
